label: Goal-relative epistemic force: force iff ordinary epistemic role and an accuracy-aiming preference
definition: For a Frame and a predicate aims on supplied preference alternatives (the accuracy or truth aim), GoalRelativeForce says: for every subject, consideration, attitude and preference d, the consideration has pro tanto force for the attitude at d iff it plays the ordinary epistemic role (assessable content, relevant application, favorable bearing; EpistemicRole) and d satisfies aims. IndifferenceAvailable says some supplied alternative fails aims: an accuracy-indifferent profile. Under this account evidence that favors p gives an accuracy-valuing subject a reason, and the same evidence gives an indifferent profile none. It differs from bare production or reward: favorable epistemic bearing is still required.
note: Stipulative analyst formulation of the strongest surviving rival recorded in docs/notes/epistemic-reasons-930.md, attribution deferred. aims is an explicit parameter, not fixed to any psychological fact. A real instrumentalist may weaken the biconditional (for example, a disjunction of goals, or goals the subject would have under reflection); this pointwise form is one tested version, not the whole family.
